tiers.smoke: Small, fast models used for first-run validation and basic test coverage.
tiers.recommended: Models that should work well on the target machine and represent the default curated experience.
tiers.advanced: Heavier or more specialized models that are supported but not part of the Milestone 1 starter catalog.

models.summary: English CTC checkpoint for forced alignment of corrected transcript text to local audio.
known_limitations: English-only character vocabulary; numerals must be written as words.
Alignment scores measure the selected acoustic path and are not calibrated word correctness probabilities.
Poor audio or text that does not match the recording can produce low scores or fail alignment.
runtime_notes: Uses a deterministic CTC Viterbi trellis against the current transcript revision.
Stores results separately from original Whisper or NeMo timing evidence.
Model weights are downloaded only after explicit user approval.

models.summary: WavLM x-vector checkpoint for local speaker similarity and provisional word-anchored diarization.
known_limitations: Cosine similarity is comparative evidence, not proof of speaker identity.
Diarization uses transcript-window clustering and does not detect overlapping speech.
Automatic cluster thresholds are dataset-dependent; speaker labels remain provisional and editable.
runtime_notes: Fine-tuned on VoxCeleb1 with an additive-margin x-vector objective.
Inputs are resampled to 16 kHz and embeddings are L2-normalized before cosine similarity.
Model weights are downloaded only after explicit user approval.

models.summary: Smallest Whisper checkpoint (39M params) for fast end-to-end offline transcription validation.
known_limitations: Lower transcription quality than larger Whisper variants.
Long-form audio should be chunked instead of processed as a single pass.
runtime_notes: Treat as the default STT smoke-test model.
Use Whisper processor-driven preprocessing.
Supports multilingual transcription and speech translation, but v1 should focus on local transcription.

models.summary: Mid-range Whisper (244M params) balancing speed and accuracy for multilingual transcription.
known_limitations: Long-form audio should be chunked into 30-second segments.
Susceptible to hallucination on silence or noisy segments.
runtime_notes: Uses standard AutoModelForSpeechSeq2Seq loading path.
Good balance between quality and resource usage for 12GB VRAM targets.
80 Mel frequency bins (same as tiny/base/medium).

models.summary: Pruned Whisper large-v3 (809M params, 4 decoder layers) — near large-v3 quality at much faster inference.
known_limitations: Uses 128 Mel bins (different from smaller variants).
Larger degradation on some languages like Thai and Cantonese vs large-v3.
Susceptible to hallucination on silence.
runtime_notes: Uses standard AutoModelForSpeechSeq2Seq loading path.
128 Mel frequency bins — processor handles this automatically.
Decoder reduced from 32 to 4 layers for significantly faster inference.
MIT licensed.

models.summary: FastConformer-TDT English ASR model used to validate first-class NeMo support.
known_limitations: English-only output.
Model card states lowercase English transcription output.
runtime_notes: Model card specifies 16000 Hz mono wav input.
Use as the default NeMo STT validation model.
Implementation should keep the NeMo loading path local-only.

models.summary: State-of-the-art 2B Conformer ASR — #1 on HuggingFace Open ASR Leaderboard (5.42% avg WER).
known_limitations: Requires explicit language tag per input — no automatic language detection.
No timestamps or speaker diarization.
Hallucination on silence — recommend VAD preprocessing.
Code-switched audio not well supported.
runtime_notes: Planned only: the upstream checkpoint requires model-supplied Python, which soundAr does not execute.
Conformer encoder-decoder architecture with 16k BPE tokenizer.
Apache 2.0 licensed.
Trained on 500k hours of curated audio-transcript pairs.

models.summary: Lightweight Voxtral 3B for speech-to-text, audio understanding, and Q&A — fits in ~9.5GB VRAM.
known_limitations: Requires transformers >= 4.54.0.
Uses chat template format for transcription requests.
8 languages only.
runtime_notes: Uses VoxtralForConditionalGeneration from transformers.
Supports transcription mode and audio Q&A mode.
Apache 2.0 licensed.
Context length 32k tokens — up to 30 min transcription.

models.summary: Compact baseline TTS path for validating the first Transformers-based synthesis flow.
known_limitations: Requires a vocoder for waveform generation.
Requires speaker embeddings for voice characteristics.
runtime_notes: Use as the default TTS smoke-test model.
Model card examples use microsoft/speecht5_hifigan plus xvector speaker embeddings.
The model, HiFi-GAN vocoder, and CMU Arctic xvector dataset are pinned to qualified revisions and kept local after download.

models.summary: Multilingual Coqui XTTS model for voice cloning and 17-language synthesis at 24kHz.
known_limitations: Heavier runtime than the smoke-test TTS path.
Voice cloning should remain optional and fully local in v1.
runtime_notes: Model card advertises support for 17 languages.
Model card advertises 24 kHz output.
Treat as a first-class engine path.

models.summary: Lightweight 82M TTS with 54 voices across 8 languages — low-latency 24kHz output.
known_limitations: Exact dependency pin and local runtime setup still need to be finalized.
Language and voice handling should be catalog- and runtime-driven.
runtime_notes: Model card usage example writes audio at 24000 Hz.
Model card release table indicates 8 languages and 54 voices.
Pin the kokoro runtime dependency during implementation.

models.summary: State-of-the-art 500M TTS with zero-shot voice cloning and emotion control — 24kHz output.
known_limitations: English-only (standard model). Multilingual variant available separately.
Requires ~8-16GB VRAM.
Built-in PerTh watermarking on all generated audio.
runtime_notes: Install via: pip install chatterbox-tts
Uses ChatterboxTTS.from_pretrained(device='cuda').
Supports exaggeration (0-1) and cfg_weight (0-1) parameters for emotion control.
Zero-shot voice cloning from ~10s reference audio.
MIT licensed.

models.summary: Lower-latency 350M English synthesis with voice cloning, paralinguistic tags, and 24kHz output.
known_limitations: English only.
The qualified Python adapter returns complete audio rather than incremental chunks.
Voice cloning requires a consent-backed reference profile.
runtime_notes: Qualified against chatterbox-tts 0.1.7.
Uses ChatterboxTurboTTS.from_local with a pinned checkpoint revision.
MIT licensed; model weights are downloaded explicitly and never bundled.

models.summary: Bilingual 3.47B speech model with natural-language voice design, expressive events, and 24 kHz output.
known_limitations: The model weights and self-hosted outputs are restricted to research and non-commercial use; commercial use requires written authorization from BreezeBlue.
Linux, CUDA, and a 12 GB NVIDIA GPU are required by the qualified eager path.
The upstream fast CUDA-graph path needs approximately 14.4 GiB and is disabled on the 12 GB target.
This first soundAr adapter exposes reference-free voice design. Upstream voice cloning and voice direction require an exact reference transcript and are not yet exposed.
runtime_notes: Uses the official eager streaming implementation pinned to source revision ca632ce6c4d05f7985da4eab29b1a5d445b43f7b.
The checkpoint contains 3,466,363,713 parameters and approximately 6.97 GB of model weights.
Supports English and Chinese plus inline vocal events such as (laugh), (cough), and (sigh).
Model weights are downloaded only after explicit user approval and are never bundled.

models.summary: Fish Audio's stable multilingual Fish Speech 1.5 checkpoint with reference-free generation and 44.1 kHz output.
known_limitations: The model weights are restricted to non-commercial use and derivatives must remain under CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0.
The official checkpoint uses PyTorch .pth files; soundAr loads them locally with weights_only=True.
This first soundAr adapter exposes reference-free generation. Voice cloning requires an exact reference transcript and is not yet exposed.
Fish Audio S2 Pro is newer, but its official runtime requires at least 24 GB VRAM and is not marked ready on this 12 GB target.

qualification.runtime: isolated Fish Speech v1.5.1 CUDA runtime

runtime_notes: Uses Fish Audio's Apache-2.0 inference source pinned to v1.5.1 commit 58046eaa1a4cefb0c8cc3a3a667b34186ea02dde.
The public checkpoint is approximately 1.47 GB and was trained on more than one million hours across 13 languages.
The official v1.5.1 inference path loads checkpoint tensors with PyTorch weights_only=True and performs no cloud inference.
Model weights are downloaded only after explicit user approval and are never bundled.

models.summary: Local 300M MusicGen model for short text-conditioned music drafts at 32 kHz.
known_limitations: This is an instrumental direction model in soundAr; it cannot condition on lyrics or reliably sing supplied text.
The model is text-to-music only in this release; melody conditioning and audio continuation are not exposed.
Generation is stochastic and can contain vocal-like artifacts even when an instrumental prompt is used.
MusicGen weights are licensed CC BY-NC 4.0 and must not be used commercially without separate permission.
Longer clips increase latency and VRAM use; this local path is bounded to 30 seconds.
runtime_notes: Uses the built-in Transformers MusicgenForConditionalGeneration implementation with local files only and no remote model code.
The engine emits a complete, atomically published WAV or FLAC artifact; streaming is intentionally not advertised.
Model weights are downloaded only after explicit user approval.

models.summary: ACE-Step 1.5 Studio: the 2B Turbo song model, 1.7B local planner, 48 kHz stereo VAE, and text encoder in one pinned local pack.
known_limitations: The complete studio pack is a large download. On a 12 GB GPU soundAr uses CPU offload so planning and decoding remain reliable.
Reference, cover, and repaint workflows require audio you own or have permission to use; soundAr records that confirmation with the request.
Stem extraction and multi-track completion use the separate ACE-Step Base Tools checkpoint.
Generated lyrics and timing should be reviewed before release; model output is not a transcript guarantee.
runtime_notes: Uses the official ACE-Step 1.5 source pinned to commit 14c0211d5a0653b0f63e27686f4c3f151b4d8629.
The 1.7B 5 Hz language model plans metadata, structure, lyrics, and semantic audio codes before the DiT render.
Supports 10-second to 10-minute generation, up to eight variations, reference audio, cover, repaint, and lyric timing.
Model weights are downloaded only after explicit user approval and remain local.

models.summary: ACE-Step Base Tools for vocal/instrument extraction, layer generation, accompaniment completion, and deeper edits.
known_limitations: This checkpoint is an editing companion, not the default song generator.
It requires the ACE-Step Studio pack for the shared VAE, text encoder, and local planner.
Base-model operations use more diffusion steps and are substantially slower than Turbo on a 12 GB GPU.
runtime_notes: Selected automatically for stem separation and multi-track tools when installed.
Uses CPU offload on 12 GB GPUs and preserves the original mix as a separate artifact.

models.summary: ACE-Step 1.5 XL Turbo quality tier for slower 48 kHz stereo renders with CPU offload.
known_limitations: The local checkpoint is approximately 11.1 GB; soundAr uses model CPU offload on 12 GB NVIDIA GPUs, which increases render time.
Lyrics are a generation condition, not a transcript guarantee; review the audible words before use.
soundAr exposes only text-to-music here: no source-audio cover, remix, repaint, or voice-reference upload is enabled.
The local workflow is bounded to 10–30 seconds and requires a CUDA GPU in this release.
runtime_notes: Uses the official local Diffusers pipeline with no remote code execution or cloud fallback.
A caption directs genre, instruments, mood, and production; optional lyrics use [Verse] and [Chorus] structure.
Model weights are downloaded only after explicit user approval and pinned to the qualified revision.
The ACE-Step weights are MIT; the bundled Qwen3 text encoder is Apache-2.0.
